metadata.note: Mount accessor endpoint not documented in provided sources; canonical operation absent.
metadata.absent_canonical_reason: No documented sys/auth mount listing endpoint in provided docs; token accessor listing is documented but does not return auth mount accessors.

metadata.note: Only documented cleanup-like delete relevant to OIDC provider docs; auth mount disable endpoint not documented in provided sources.

oidc_jwt.description: A valid Vault bearer token can be reused across multiple API calls until expiry or revocation.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault token auth lookup-self docs and RFC 6750 bearer semantics
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated use of the same unexpired session token as replay when num_uses is unlimited.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT not-before handling may be effectively optional or tolerant because not_before_leeway defaults to 150 seconds when set to 0 and can be disabled with -1.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of a slightly future nbf token may be by design under default leeway; tighten leeway before testing.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT nbf enforcement is role-dependent and can be effectively relaxed by configured leeway; absence of strict nbf rejection is not necessarily a vulnerability.
oidc_jwt.note: Vault adds default not-before leeway unless disabled with -1, so near-future nbf acceptance can be by design.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT not-before handling has configurable leeway and can disable added leeway with -1; acceptance behavior around absent nbf is not necessarily a bug because nbf is optional.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat acceptance of tokens without nbf as a vulnerability by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's OIDC provider authorization endpoint documents nonce as optional, though strongly encouraged.
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of nonce alone is not sufficient to report a vulnerability without a concrete replay or substitution impact.

oidc_jwt.description: Old signing keys may remain accepted until verification_ttl expires after OIDC key rotation.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag acceptance of tokens signed by a rotated-out key before verification_ttl expiry.

oidc_jwt.description: When an admin reconfigures JWT validation trust settings such as jwks_url, oidc_discovery_url, jwt_validation_pubkeys, or bound_issuer, logins under the new trust anchor are expected.
oidc_jwt.note: Admin-authorized trust anchor changes are by design; only flag continued acceptance of the old trust anchor after the change should have taken effect.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's OIDC provider does not support request or request_uri parameters.
oidc_jwt.note: Rejecting or ignoring OIDC request objects is expected; request-object signature tests do not apply.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's documented OIDC provider metadata reports request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not run request-object signature tests such as oidc_request_object_alg_none against this provider surface; unsupported request objects are not a validation bypass.

oidc_jwt.description: A Vault OIDC provider client with no assignments allows no Vault entities to authenticate.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc-provider Create or update a client
oidc_jwt.note: Authentication failure in this state is expected and not an authorization bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Identity group policies may apply across namespace boundaries when the global group_policy_application_mode is set to 'any'.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-namespace policy inheritance is documented behavior in this mode, not an authorization escalation bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Confidential OIDC clients may use PKCE but are not required to; only public clients must use PKCE.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client
oidc_jwt.note: A missing code_verifier for a confidential client is not by itself a bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias name, potentially sharing privileges; Vault explicitly warns about alias reuse cardinality.
oidc_jwt.note: Tests should distinguish documented alias-reuse behavior from unintended identity collisions.

oidc_jwt.constraint: configure_jwt_validation requires exactly one trust source: set ONE of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Do NOT set more than one or none; test setup is invalid otherwise.
create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. A role with no bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims is invalid test setup.

For jwt roles, if the JWT contains an aud claim, bound_audiences is required and must match at least one aud value. For I1/I5 audience tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly configure bound_audiences on jwt roles; otherwise failures or passes may reflect invalid setup rather than audience enforcement.
clock_skew_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 60 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables leeway. Never assume 0 means strict checking.
expiration_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables leeway. Never assume 0 means strict expiration enforcement.
not_before_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables leeway. Never assume 0 means strict nbf enforcement.

For I2 expired_token tests on jwt roles, set expiration_leeway to -1 to remove the default 150-second grace period. Leaving it at 0 silently enables the default and can make slightly expired tokens pass by design.

For I2 future_token/nbf tests on jwt roles, set not_before_leeway to -1 to remove the default 150-second grace period. Leaving it at 0 silently enables the default and can make future-nbf tokens pass by design.
For I2 clock-skew-sensitive tests on jwt roles, set clock_skew_leeway to -1 to disable the default 60-second global skew allowance. Leaving it at 0 silently enables the default.

When testing I1 issuer validation, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer unless the test intentionally verifies issuer is unbound. Without bound_issuer, Vault does not compare the iss claim, so issuer-substitution tests become meaningless.

bound_subject supports exact string match only; there is no companion type parameter. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting a wildcard.

bound_audiences is documented only as list membership against aud claims; there is no companion type parameter. Treat it as exact matching only. For cross-identity or cross-provider tests, do NOT use wildcard audience values; either set exact audiences or omit the constraint when the scenario requires multiple different audiences to pass.

user_claim must resolve to a string. If the selected claim is non-string, login will fail as invalid setup rather than demonstrating an identity-binding issue. For I4 tests, choose a claim that is always a string, typically sub or another stable string claim.
groups_claim must resolve to a list of strings. Sending a scalar string instead of a string array is invalid setup and can confound I4/I5 group-mapping tests.

bound_claims supports string, integer, boolean, or list-of-strings expected values, and bound_claims_type controls matching semantics. In the default string mode, values are treated as literals and must match exactly; in glob mode, '*' is wildcard. For I4 multi-identity tests, omit exact-match bound_claims constraints rather than using '*' unless bound_claims_type is explicitly set to glob.

For I5 numeric coercion tests involving bound_claims, set bound_claims_type to glob rather than the default string so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings for matching instead of being rejected outright. Then test integer bound value N against JWT float N+0.7 to detect truncation/coercion bugs.

For I2 token-freshness tests against JWT login, include a control login using a valid token (for example exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}}, sub={{jwt_sub}}) alongside the attack token. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken trust-anchor or role setup.

OIDC callback tests must preserve the exact state and nonce values issued in the prior auth_url response flow. The callback endpoint requires both state and nonce, and optional client_nonce must match the value supplied to auth_url. Mixing values across sessions is invalid setup except when intentionally testing flow binding.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request and OIDC callback

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, omit the role parameter on login_with_jwt so Vault uses default_role. Supplying an explicit role bypasses the default-role behavior and invalidates the test.

For I3 jwt_role_config_tighten_reauth tests, modify_role_config must tighten constraints such as adding bound_claims or narrowing bound_audiences. Do NOT remove constraints or broaden values, as that changes authorization in the permissive direction and cannot demonstrate stale enforcement.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests using jwks_url or jwt_validation_pubkeys, the second login must reuse the same role and same claims while only the trusted key material changes. Otherwise a failure may be caused by role drift rather than trust-anchor rotation.

Vault OIDC provider clients allow no entities by default: if assignments is empty, no Vault entities are allowed to authenticate through the client. To permit all entities in provider-flow tests, supply the built-in allow_all assignment or an assignment that includes the target entities/groups.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc-provider Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each authorization request. Any mismatch is rejected by design and should not be interpreted as a flow-coherence bug.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc-provider Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider public clients must use PKCE: code_challenge is required at authorize time and code_verifier is required at token time. Confidential clients may use PKCE optionally. Tests that omit PKCE for public clients are invalid setup.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc-provider Authorization endpoint and Token endpoint

oidc_jwt.constraint: Vault's OIDC provider discovery document states request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT run OIDC request-object attacks (including alg=none request JWTs) against this provider endpoint; unsupported request parameters are not a vulnerability signal here.

For OIDC provider replay-mitigation tests, always send a nonce in the authorization request even though the parameter is documented as optional. The docs strongly encourage it and the nonce is returned in the ID token; omitting it weakens the test oracle for replay-related checks.
KV v2 max_versions has sentinel semantics: value 0 or unset does NOT mean keep zero versions; it means keep the platform default of 10 versions. Never assume 0 disables version retention.
KV v2 delete_version_after has sentinel semantics: value "0s" means no automatic deletion timer. Do not confuse it with immediate deletion.
verify_read_secret on KV v2 MUST use the /data/ path segment (/v1/{engine}/data/{path}). Using the mount root path hits the wrong API shape and returns misleading 404s.
KV v2 list operations use /metadata/ paths, not /data/. If the fuzzer needs to list seeded resources, grant list capability on /metadata/ even when reads and writes use /data/.

External identity groups used for JWT/OIDC group alias mapping should be created as type=external. Group aliases map external group names onto internal group objects; using the wrong group type can distort group-policy tests.

Group policy escalation tests must account for the global /sys/config/group-policy-application mode. In the default within_namespace_hierarchy mode, group policies only apply within the namespace hierarchy; in any mode, they apply regardless of namespace hierarchy. Do not flag cross-namespace policy differences without checking this setting.

Entity alias names are security-sensitive identifiers. Vault docs explicitly warn that alias reuse can bind multiple authenticated entities to the same alias and share privileges. For I4 collision tests, use unique alias names per entity unless intentionally testing alias-collision behavior.

Exactly one of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, and jwt_validation_pubkeys must be set on /v1/auth/{mount}/config. The fuzzer MUST NOT send more than one trust source or omit all of them, or setup will fail before any JWT validation test runs.

bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. For issuer-validation tests, the fuzzer MUST use oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys if it needs bound_issuer enforcement; do not combine issuer binding with jwks_pairs.

Every JWT/OIDC role requires at least one bound value to be set. The fuzzer MUST configure at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, bound_claims, or another documented bound constraint, otherwise role creation/update is invalid.

For JWT roles, bound_audiences is required when the JWT contains an aud claim and must match at least one aud value. For I1/I5 audience tests, the control role MUST include bound_audiences; omitting it can make audience-mismatch tests pass trivially because no audience check was configured.
clock_skew_leeway has special sentinels: value 0 means use the default 60 seconds of leeway, while value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict zero-skew checking.
expiration_leeway has special sentinels: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds of leeway, while value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 means immediate expiration enforcement.
not_before_leeway has special sentinels: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds of leeway, while value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict nbf enforcement.

bound_subject supports exact string match only; there is no companion type parameter for wildcard or glob matching. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST omit bound_subject entirely rather than setting '*' or another pattern, because '*' would only match the literal subject '*'.

bound_audiences is exact list-membership matching only; there is no companion type parameter for glob or regex. For cross-provider or multi-audience tests, the fuzzer MUST supply concrete audience values and MUST NOT use wildcard patterns expecting broad matches.

user_claim names the claim used as the entity alias and must resolve to a string. If user_claim_json_pointer is false, the value is treated as a literal claim name, not a JSON pointer. The fuzzer MUST set user_claim_json_pointer=true when testing nested claims via JSON pointer syntax, otherwise the lookup targets the wrong claim and identity-binding results are uninterpretable.

groups_claim must resolve to a list of strings and supports JSON pointer syntax. The fuzzer MUST send groups as an array of strings for group-alias and policy-escalation tests; sending a scalar string is a type mismatch and may fail before any authorization-binding behavior is exercised.

bound_claims matching mode is controlled by bound_claims_type. If bound_claims_type='string' (default), values are treated as literals and must match exactly. If bound_claims_type='glob', '*' matches any number of characters. For I4 multi-identity scenarios that need multiple distinct values to pass the same constraint, the fuzzer MUST either omit the exact-match constraint or explicitly set bound_claims_type='glob'; do not set bound_claims={'sub':'*'} under the default string mode because that matches only the literal '*'.

bound_claims accepts expected values as string, integer, boolean, or list of strings, but the default bound_claims_type='string' treats values as literals and must match exactly. For I5 numeric coercion tests, the fuzzer SHOULD set bound_claims_type='glob' so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings for matching rather than being rejected outright by strict literal handling.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer. Without bound_issuer, Vault documents issuer comparison as optional and the test may falsely conclude issuer validation is bypassed when it was never configured.

For I2 expired_token tests on JWT roles, the fuzzer MUST account for Vault's default expiration_leeway of 150 seconds when the role sets 0 or leaves it unset. To test strict expiry rejection, set expiration_leeway=-1 or place exp sufficiently far in the past beyond the default buffer; otherwise an apparently expired token may still be accepted by design.

For I2 future_token tests on JWT roles, the fuzzer MUST account for Vault's default not_before_leeway of 150 seconds when the role sets 0 or leaves it unset. To test strict nbf rejection, set not_before_leeway=-1 or place nbf sufficiently far in the future beyond the default buffer.

For I2 freshness tests, include a control login using a valid JWT alongside the attack token. A failed JWT login without a control cannot distinguish expired/nbf rejection from broken trust-source or role configuration.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, changing jwks_url, oidc_discovery_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys is an admin-authorized trust-anchor change. The oracle MUST only flag continued acceptance of the old key after the new configuration should apply; acceptance of the new trust anchor itself is by design.

For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, login_with_jwt may omit role and then uses default_role from mount config. The fuzzer MUST omit the role parameter on both baseline and post-change logins when testing default_role behavior; supplying an explicit role bypasses the default-role code path entirely.

For OIDC-flow coherence tests, allowed_redirect_uris on the role and redirect_uri supplied to /v1/auth/{mount}/oidc/auth_url must match the callback used later. A mismatch is expected rejection, not a flow-binding vulnerability.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt Create/Update role and OIDC auth_url

oidc_jwt.constraint: Vault's OIDC auth_url endpoint returns a Vault-generated auth_url rather than acting as a standard /authorize endpoint. The fuzzer MUST treat start_oidc_auth as a preparatory step that yields state/nonce embedded in auth_url, and exchange_code_for_token MUST use the exact state and nonce from that flow. Mixing values across sessions is the intended state-swap/code-injection test; arbitrary values will just break setup.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request and callback

oidc_jwt.constraint: Vault documents nonce on the provider authorization endpoint as optional but strongly encouraged. For OIDC relying-party tests against Vault's identity/oidc/provider endpoints, the fuzzer MUST include nonce in authorization requests when testing replay resistance; absence of nonce weakens the test oracle because the platform may legitimately omit nonce binding if the client did not request it.

Public OIDC clients must use PKCE for the authorization code flow, while confidential clients may use it optionally. For PKCE tests, the fuzzer MUST create the client with client_type='public' when it expects code_verifier to be mandatory; otherwise missing code_verifier may be accepted by design for confidential clients.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: At the OIDC provider token endpoint, client_id is required for public clients and for confidential clients using client_secret_post; Authorization: Basic is only for confidential clients using client_secret_basic. The fuzzer MUST align token-endpoint authentication style with client_type or failures will reflect client-auth misconfiguration, not security enforcement.

redirect_uris on an OIDC client must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each authentication request. For redirect_uri mismatch tests, the control flow MUST use an exact configured URI and the attack flow MUST vary only the redirect_uri; otherwise both flows may fail for setup reasons.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC client TTL fields id_token_ttl and access_token_ttl default to 24h when omitted. The fuzzer MUST set explicit short TTLs when testing token freshness or expiry behavior; relying on defaults will produce long-lived tokens and weak I2 coverage.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: KV v2 engine config max_versions uses a sentinel: value 0 or unset does not mean keep zero versions; it means keep 10 versions. Never assume 0 disables version retention.
KV v2 engine delete_version_after uses a sentinel: value '0s' means no automatic timed deletion, not immediate deletion. Never assume '0s' causes instant expiry of secret versions.
verify_read_secret on KV v2 MUST use the /data/ path segment. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and returns misleading 404s unrelated to authorization.

KV v2 list operations require permissions on the /metadata/ path even when reads and writes use /data/. The fuzzer MUST grant list capability on /metadata/ if it needs secret enumeration; otherwise list failures are policy-shape issues, not authorization-binding bugs.

Vault token num_uses limits every API call made with that token, including verify_granted_identity via /v1/auth/token/lookup-self and verify_read_secret. Minimum safe value is 2 if the sequence performs one self-lookup and one protected-resource read after login; use 3+ if additional session-bound verification calls are included.

Identity group aliases are the documented mechanism for mapping external groups into Vault identity groups. For JWT/OIDC group-policy tests, the fuzzer MUST create external groups as type='external' groups plus group aliases bound to the auth mount accessor, rather than manually stuffing member_entity_ids into the group and expecting upstream group-claim mapping semantics.

The global /v1/sys/config/group-policy-application mode changes whether identity-group policies apply only within namespace hierarchy or across any namespace. For I5 group_policy_escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST record this mode and avoid flagging cross-namespace group policy application as a bug when the mode is set to 'any'.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids defaults to allowing no clients when empty, while '*' allows all clients. For audience/client-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST set allowed_client_ids explicitly; leaving it empty causes blanket denial that can mask the behavior under test.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider Create or update a provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC client assignments default to allowing no Vault entities. To permit authentication through a client, the fuzzer MUST either attach explicit assignment resources or use the built-in allow_all assignment for broad controls. Otherwise authorization failures occur before token issuance and are not audience/scope bugs.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client and identity/oidc/assignment docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: configure_jwt_validation requires exactly one trust source: set exactly one of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Do not send multiple trust sources in the same config or setup will be invalid.
configure_jwt_validation: bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. For issuer-validation tests, do not use jwks_pairs if the test needs bound_issuer enforcement.

For JWT roles, if the JWT contains an aud claim, bound_audiences is required and at least one configured audience must match one of the JWT aud values. Do not run audience-validation tests without explicitly configuring bound_audiences.

user_claim must resolve to a string claim value. groups_claim must resolve to a list of strings. Tests using non-string user claims or non-list groups claims will fail as type errors rather than exposing authorization bugs.
Numeric sentinel semantics: clock_skew_leeway value 0 means use default 60 seconds, not strict zero; value -1 disables added leeway. Never assume 0 means no skew allowance.
Numeric sentinel semantics: expiration_leeway value 0 means use default 150 seconds, not strict zero; value -1 disables added leeway. Never assume 0 means immediate exp enforcement with no buffer.

Numeric sentinel semantics: not_before_leeway value 0 means use default 150 seconds, not strict zero; value -1 disables added leeway. Never assume 0 disables nbf checking or means exact-time enforcement.

bound_audiences is exact audience membership matching only; there is no companion type parameter for glob or regex. For cross-provider or multi-identity tests that need varying aud values, do not use wildcard strings in bound_audiences because they will not act as patterns.

bound_claims matching semantics depend on bound_claims_type. If bound_claims_type is 'string' (default), values are treated as literals and must match exactly. If bound_claims_type is 'glob', '*' matches any number of characters. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, omit exact-match bound_claims rather than using '*' unless bound_claims_type is explicitly set to 'glob'.

For I5 numeric coercion tests on bound_claims, set bound_claims_type='glob' rather than the default 'string' so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings for matching instead of being rejected outright. bound_claims accepts string, integer, boolean, or list values.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on JWT roles, include a control login using a valid token in the same setup. Otherwise a failed attack login may be caused by broken trust-source or role configuration rather than time-claim enforcement.

OIDC auth flow tests must keep redirect_uri exactly consistent: the redirect_uri used at the token endpoint must exactly match the redirect_uri used when the authorization code was generated, and it must be one of the configured redirect URIs.
Vault OIDC provider authorization requests require scope to include 'openid'. Tests omitting openid are invalid setup, not security findings.

For Vault as OIDC provider, public clients must use PKCE: code_challenge is required at authorize and code_verifier is required at token. Confidential clients may omit PKCE. Do not interpret public-client rejection without PKCE as a bug.

Vault OIDC provider documents nonce as optional but strongly encouraged. Acceptance of requests without nonce is not by itself a vulnerability unless the test specifically demonstrates replay or token substitution in a flow that should have been nonce-bound.

OIDC provider client assignments default to denying all Vault entities. To allow authentication through a client, configure assignments explicitly; to allow all entities, use the built-in allow_all assignment. Otherwise login failures are expected setup failures.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider allowed_client_ids on the provider defaults to allowing no clients when empty; '*' allows all clients. Do not treat empty allowed_client_ids as permissive.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider Create or update a provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each authentication request. Wildcards are not documented; use exact URIs only.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 config-change tests on default role behavior, login_without_role uses the auth mount's default_role. After changing default_role in configure_jwt_validation, new logins are expected to bind to the new role. This is by design; only stale use of the old default after reconfiguration is a coherence issue.

For I3 key-rotation or trust-anchor change tests, new logins must be evaluated against the updated configure_jwt_validation settings immediately. A success under the new admin-configured trust source is by design; only continued acceptance under the old trust source after reconfiguration is suspicious.

External identity groups used for JWT/OIDC group aliasing should be mapped via group aliases. Group alias names are the external group names from groups_claim, and canonical_id must point to the internal group. This is the correct setup path for group-based policy tests.

Group policy application mode can broaden effective permissions across namespaces when set to 'any'. For I5 group_policy_escalation tests, first read /sys/config/group-policy-application and account for 'any' as global cross-namespace group policy application by design.

KV v2 list operations require list capability on the /metadata/ path even if reads and writes use /data/. Missing metadata-path permissions cause setup or verification failures unrelated to JWT/OIDC authorization logic.

Numeric sentinel semantics: KV v2 engine max_versions value 0 means keep 10 versions, not zero versions. delete_version_after value '0s' means no automatic timed deletion. Do not assume zero disables storage or causes immediate deletion.

KV v2 write CAS semantics: options.cas=0 only allows create-if-absent; for existing or soft-deleted keys, cas must match the current version. Avoid CAS-related failures when seeding or mutating protected resources unless the test is specifically about CAS behavior.

Session-use budget: Vault tokens can be configured with token_num_uses/num_uses via token fields on auth roles. Every API call made with the session token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret, consumes a use. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret read, minimum safe value is 2; use 3+ if additional session-bound verification calls are present.
oidc_jwt.source: tokenfields referenced by auth/jwt role + auth/token lookup-self

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider token endpoint only supports grant_type=authorization_code in the documented provider flow. Do not attempt RFC8693 token exchange against this endpoint; such tests are invalid for the documented Vault OIDC provider APIs.
